content:
I am working on a Halloween show and a returning guest writes “I was about 19 years old at the time, and I was a volunteer firefighter in an area called Reserve Mines. One night, around 2:00 or 2:30 in the morning, our pagers went off. A neighboring town was calling for assistance because a large warehouse was on fire.

We did what we always did. We jumped on the fire truck and headed out. By the time we arrived, it was around 3:00 a.m., and the place was completely ablaze. It was a major structure fire, and we needed a lot of resources to get it under control.

At one point during the night, my fire chief came over to me and said, “Go back down that road and see if you can find a fire hydrant. Let me know if there’s one down there.”

The road we were on wasn’t too far outside of town, just on the outskirts of Dominion. It was a small dirt road, almost more like a driveway than an actual road. It was only about a quarter of a kilometer long.

So I set off on my own, walking down this dark road. There was nobody around. It was just me and the pitch-black darkness.

I was about halfway down the road, looking left and right for a fire hydrant, when a man suddenly appeared.

He was dressed in a full firefighter’s uniform. He had a big beard and a chiseled face, a very distinctive look about him. He seemed to come out of nowhere, but I wasn’t particularly startled. I figured he was just another firefighter I hadn’t met before.

He approached me and said, “Hey, John,” calling me by my first and middle name.

Then he started asking me questions about things nobody else knew. He knew I was thinking about going into law enforcement and asked about my plans for a career in policing. He seemed to know all kinds of personal things about me that I hadn’t shared with anyone.

It was really bizarre. There I was, 19 years old, standing alone in the middle of the night while we were fighting a major structure fire, trying to figure out how this guy knew so much about me.

After we’d talked for a bit, he pointed up above me and said, “John, you need to be careful. Those wires up there are attached to that building. When those walls collapse, that power line is coming down. You’d better get out of here.”

I looked up, and what he was saying made perfect sense. The building was burning, and there was a real possibility that the walls could collapse and bring the power line down with them.

Then he said, “Oh, and the fire hydrant? You’ll find it about 100 feet that way.”

I said, “Geez, thank you very much.”

I started walking toward the hydrant, and it wasn’t even 30 seconds later that I heard people yelling and screaming.

The exact thing he’d warned me about had happened. The power line came down and hit the ground.

I remember thinking, “Wow! That fella really called that one.”

Two days later, I was back at the fire station and talking with my fire chief. I told him, “I met a guy during that fire who gave me a great heads-up. He told me to get the hell out of the road because that power line was going to come down. I’d really love to know who he was. He was an awful nice man, and he seemed to know everything about me.”

My fire chief had been around for years. He knew everybody in the area and was familiar with the neighboring fire departments, so I figured he’d know who I was talking about.

He asked me to describe the man. I did my best to explain what he looked like: the big beard, the chiseled face, and that distinctive appearance.

My chief looked at me and said, “Yeah, John. That guy passed away about a year ago. He had a massive heart attack. You’re describing him exactly.”

I didn’t know what to say.

After that, I had other occasions to work with the neighboring fire department, and I kept looking for this guy. I asked around, trying to find out who he was, but there was no such member of the department other than the man who had passed away.

I eventually saw a picture of him. Now, keep in mind, it was about 3:00 in the morning, and I was standing on a dark road in the middle of a major fire. But when I saw that picture, I knew the face.

If that wasn’t the man who had spoken to me that night, it was his twin. So who knows? Maybe it was a real person who somehow knew me. I can’t explain it.

But I’ll tell you, Wes, it was some weird, weird stuff.”
